title: Redis Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Redis course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: What does GET need to find the value?
questions.explanation: A key is a name used to find a value. SET stores a string, and GET reads that string back.

questions.question: What does INCR add?
questions.explanation: INCR adds one to a key holding an integer. Redis performs that increment as one command.

questions.question: What does EX 30 mean?
questions.explanation: An expiry makes a key disappear after a time limit. It is useful for temporary data such as a short-lived cached answer.

questions.question: What does DEL remove here?
questions.explanation: EXISTS checks for a key without reading its value. DEL removes the named key.

questions.question: Which two names does HGET use?
questions.explanation: A hash stores several named fields under one Redis key. It can hold a small record such as a book title and page count.

questions.question: Which item leaves this queue first?
questions.explanation: A Redis list keeps values in order. Adding on the right and removing on the left gives first-in, first-out behaviour.

questions.question: What does SCARD count?
questions.explanation: A set holds unique members without a promised order. Adding a duplicate does not make another copy.

questions.question: What decides the sorted order here?
options: Only the length of each name
questions.explanation: A sorted set pairs each member with a score. Redis can return members ordered by that score.

questions.question: When is a full SCAN iteration finished?
options: After exactly ten keys every time
questions.explanation: SCAN walks through key names using a cursor. It is safer for large keyspaces than asking for every matching key in one blocking command.

questions.question: Does MULTI provide ordinary SQL-style rollback?
options: Yes, every runtime error undoes all commands
No, its transaction rules are different
questions.explanation: MULTI queues commands for EXEC. Redis runs that queued group without another client's commands between them.

questions.question: Will a late subscriber receive an old pub/sub message?
options: No, plain pub/sub has no replay history
Yes, every message is saved forever
questions.explanation: Publish/subscribe sends live messages to clients currently listening to a channel. It is not a stored message history.

questions.question: What determines restart durability?
options: The configured persistence and backup design
questions.explanation: Redis persistence settings decide how data is written to disk. A cache may be rebuildable, while important records need a deliberate durability plan.
